reason: Spin-down comes from magnetic torque and glitches from superfluid vortices; neither is rigid-body dynamics. Free-precession detections are contested.

fix.breaks: Superfluid interiors with pinned vortices and elastic crusts invalidate a single rigid body; spin-down and glitches are not rigid-body effects.

reason: The claim that the Moon's stabilisation of obliquity matters for habitability is contested (Lissauer et al. 2012); obliquity cycles also need secular orbital forcing.

fix.breaks: Lissauer et al. (2012) find a moonless Earth's obliquity varies far less than Laskar's chaotic estimates; the link from obliquity to habitability is model-dependent.

reason: Vlasov is a mean-field closure in which H depends on f. It fails when correlations or collisions matter, so it is not an identity with N-particle Liouville.

fix.summary: The collisionless Vlasov equation is the one-particle Liouville equation in the self-consistent mean field, df/dt={f,H[f]}=0, so phase-space density is conserved along characteristics. It has a Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian field structure (Morrison–Marsden).
fix.breaks: It is a truncation of the BBGKY hierarchy: it drops correlations and collisions and is nonlinear through H[f].

reason: A correct but one-sided method transfer, so not structural in a mechanics course; the summary overgeneralises.

reason: Too generic as written; make it the specific statement that MHD adds Maxwell stress to the fluid momentum equation plus induction.

fix.breaks: ω=∇×u is slaved to the flow while B is independent and back-reacts through the Lorentz force; unmagnetised fluids have no Alfvén waves.

reason: Duplicate of C0830; the HED laboratory-astrophysics content is absorbed there.

reason: Planetary and stellar dynamos are driven by rotating spherical-shell convection, not plane Rayleigh–Bénard; the solar dynamo also relies on shear (Ω-effect).

fix.summary: Rotating thermal and compositional convection in Earth's outer core drives the geodynamo, and convection-zone flows drive the solar dynamo. Helical, Coriolis-organised convective motions supply the mean-field α-effect, while differential rotation supplies the Ω-effect.

reason: Absorbs C0834: Kelvin–Helmholtz on the magnetopause flanks as a magnetised-KH example.

fix.summary: Interchange instability is Rayleigh–Taylor with effective gravity from field-line curvature. Magnetic tension raises Kelvin–Helmholtz thresholds (as on the magnetopause flanks), and Chandrasekhar's magnetoconvection shows the field raising the critical Rayleigh number.

reason: Nyquist methods did not originate in plasma physics. The real specific link is Landau resonance ↔ shear-flow critical layer and Penrose ↔ Rayleigh inflection criteria.

fix.name: Landau damping and inviscid shear-flow critical layers
fix.summary: Linearised Vlasov and inviscid 2D shear flow (Rayleigh equation) are mathematically parallel: Landau resonance maps to the critical layer, the Case–van Kampen continuum to the shear-flow continuous spectrum, and Penrose's criterion to Rayleigh–Fjørtoft inflection-point criteria (Briggs, Daugherty & Levy 1970).
fix.breaks: The resonance lies in velocity space for plasmas and in physical space for shear flows; kinetic instabilities with no fluid counterpart remain.

reason: Duplicate of C0832 (magnetised KH/RT); the name also mismatches the content.
The map drops the drift (β-like) term that defines Hasegawa–Mima; the summary should state the Rossby-wave isomorphism and dual cascade.

fix.summary: The Hasegawa–Mima equation for drift waves is isomorphic to the Charney–Obukhov equation for Rossby waves. Both show the 2D dual cascade (inverse energy, forward enstrophy) and spontaneous zonal flows, so tokamak zonal flows parallel Jovian jets.

reason: Cut the filler about the accretion-disk paper; a broad mechanism link is overrated at 3.

fix.summary: Turbulent flows stretch, twist and fold field lines: above a critical magnetic Reynolds number they act as small-scale dynamos, and helical turbulence gives the mean-field α-effect with turbulent diffusivity η_t.

reason: Absorbs C0838 (critical balance). The MHD cascade is local in k⊥, so the 'non-local' claim is wrong; this is a transfer of phenomenology.

fix.breaks: A strong mean field makes the cascade anisotropic; dynamic-alignment theories (Boldyrev) predict k⊥^{-3/2}, and which spectrum holds is contested.

reason: Duplicate of C0837 (critical balance absorbed there).

fix.summary: Rankine–Hugoniot jump conditions are integral mass, momentum and energy conservation across a thin discontinuity. Collisionless shocks obey MHD versions of them, with dissipation from wave–particle fields instead of collisions.
fix.breaks: Magnetic terms, pressure anisotropy and escaping accelerated particles modify the hydrodynamic jump conditions.

reason: Generic: names no amplitude equation, wavelength-selection mechanism or shared technique; as its own breaks concedes, there is no real mapping.

fix.breaks: Kuramoto coupling is all-to-all on a circle, with no spatial structure or Poisson equation; damping requires smooth frequency distributions.

reason: Plasma crystals and their measured phonon spectra date from the 1990s and early 2000s, so they are established; clean up the summary wording.

fix.summary: Dusty-plasma crystals are screened-Coulomb (Yukawa) lattices whose phonon dispersion relations, measured by video tracking of individual grains, match normal-mode lattice theory.

reason: A textbook sheet-model picture; cold Langmuir oscillations are dispersionless, so 'continuum of coupled oscillators' overstates the link.

fix.summary: In the cold sheet model, displaced electron sheets oscillate harmonically at ω_p; thermal pressure couples them, giving Bohm–Gross dispersion ω²=ω_p²+3k²v_th².

reason: It is the same averaging theorem (Landau–Lifshitz effective potential) applied to both, which makes it a mechanism; relativistic intensities break the simple form.

fix.breaks: Requires ω much faster than the slow motion; at relativistic intensities (a0≳1) the ponderomotive force changes form.

reason: Absorbs C0862 (wave speeds and tomography); add the anelastic and anisotropic limits.

fix.name: Mantle convection as high-Ra Rayleigh–Bénard
fix.summary: Mantle convection is infinite-Prandtl Rayleigh–Bénard convection, heated internally and from below, at Ra~10^7, far above Ra_c; it drives plate motion, with subducting slabs as the cold downwellings.
fix.breaks: Mantle rheology is strongly temperature-dependent and non-Newtonian; plates are brittle lids, not free-slip boundaries.

fix.breaks: There is no rotating mass: spin expectation values obey the classical equation because it is linear; relaxation is phenomenological.

fix.summary: Surface gravity waves obey ω²=gk tanh(kh): in deep water ω²=gk with c_g=c_p/2; in shallow water c=√(gh) is nondispersive, governing tides and tsunamis.

record.name: Resonance chaos clears Kirkwood gaps
record.summary: Chaotic zones around Jupiter mean-motion resonances (Wisdom's 3:1 analysis) pump asteroid eccentricities until orbits cross Mars, clearing the Kirkwood gaps; secular resonance overlap also gives the inner planets ~5 Myr Lyapunov times (Laskar).

record.name: Resonant magnetic perturbations and edge stochasticity
record.summary: Applied resonant magnetic perturbations open island chains on rational q surfaces; when neighbouring islands overlap (Chirikov criterion), the edge field becomes stochastic. This is used to suppress ELMs, though the transport mechanism is still debated.

record.name: Solar convection zone and Schwarzschild criterion
record.summary: The outer ~30% of the Sun convects because its radiative temperature gradient exceeds the adiabatic one (Schwarzschild criterion, the inviscid buoyancy limit of Rayleigh–Bénard at enormous Ra). Granulation is the surface cells, and helioseismology locates the zone's base.
